intro.text: This entry describes auriculocondylar syndrome-4 (ARCND4). I cannot reliably recall the causal gene, its zygosity, or the reports that defined this form, so the number-sign formula is not used here.

paragraphs.text: Auriculocondylar syndrome is a craniofacial malformation disorder of the first and second pharyngeal arches. Its cardinal features are malformed external ears, typically a 'question mark' ear with a cleft between the helix and the lobule, and hypoplasia of the mandibular condyle with temporomandibular joint abnormalities and micrognathia. Other features can include round face, prominent cheeks, microstomia, glossoptosis, and respiratory or feeding difficulties in infancy. Expressivity is variable, both within and between families.

paragraphs.text: Auriculocondylar syndrome is genetically heterogeneous. Other forms that I recall with confidence are ARCND1, caused by mutation in the GNAI3 gene; ARCND2, caused by mutation in the PLCB4 gene; and ARCND3, caused by mutation in the EDN1 gene. All of these genes act in the endothelin-1/endothelin receptor type A signaling pathway, which patterns the mandibular arch.

checks.claim: Auriculocondylar syndrome is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: our results led to the mapping of a first locus of ACS (ACS1) and also showed evidence for genetic heterogeneity, suggesting that there are at least two loci responsible for this phenotype.
checks.explanation: The paper reports evidence for genetic heterogeneity, with at least two loci.

checks.claim: Auriculocondylar syndrome-1 (ARCND1) is caused by mutation in the GNAI3 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: The most commonly mutated gene in individuals with ARCND is PLCB4 (MIM 600810; 58% of patients), followed by GNAI3 (MIM 139370; 19% of cases)
checks.explanation: GNAI3 is named as a causative gene, but the paper does not identify which form (ARCND1) it causes.

checks.claim: Auriculocondylar syndrome-2 (ARCND2) is caused by mutation in the PLCB4 gene.

checks.explanation: PLCB4 is named as a causative gene, but the paper does not identify it with ARCND2.

checks.claim: Auriculocondylar syndrome-3 (ARCND3) is caused by mutation in the EDN1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: followed by GNAI3 (MIM 139370; 19% of cases) and EDN1 (MIM 131240 and MIM 139370; 15% of cases)
checks.explanation: EDN1 is named as a causative gene, but the paper does not identify it with ARCND3.

checks.claim: GNAI3, PLCB4, and EDN1 all act in the endothelin-1/endothelin receptor type A signaling pathway.
checks.evidence_quote: So far, pathogenic variants in patients with ARCND have been found in genes of the EDN1-endothelin-1 receptor type A (EDNRA) pathway
checks.explanation: The known ARCND genes are placed in the EDN1-EDNRA pathway.

checks.claim: The endothelin-1/endothelin receptor type A signaling pathway patterns the mandibular arch.
checks.evidence_quote: which are expressed by the neural crest-derived ectomesenchymal cells of pharyngeal arches and are responsible for the patterning of the mandibular domain in the first arch.
checks.explanation: The paper states that the pathway patterns the mandibular domain.
